_how_to_edit: The story page reads this file on every load. See outages/UPDATE.md. Times are hours on an Eastern clock counted from midnight starting Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026 (35.5 = 11:30 a.m. Friday, Nov. 13; 131 = 11 a.m. Tuesday, Nov. 17).
headline_status: NSA Net was still down at last report, and the agency blamed “scheduled routine maintenance”
nsa_start_label: first reported by about 11 a.m. Eastern Tuesday

outages.name: Microsoft 365
outages.label: About 24 hours
outages.note: Exchange Online failed at about 11:17 a.m. Eastern on Thursday, Nov. 12. Microsoft's preliminary report puts the outage at nearly 24 hours, and it said the last affected customers were restored early Saturday. It blamed a software defect exposed by network work, not an attack.

outages.name: FAA ground stop
outages.label: 4 hr 21 min
outages.note: The FAA halted every departure at 3:54 p.m. Eastern on Friday, Nov. 13, and lifted the stop at 8:15 p.m. FlightAware counted about 9,200 cancellations. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a router overloaded while contractor L3Harris moved FAA lines from copper to fiber, but said the fault was not yet determined. The FBI is giving technical support to the review.

outages.name: Workday
outages.label: Back by Saturday
outages.note: Outage reports jumped just after 5 p.m. Eastern on Friday, Nov. 13. Workday said service was restored by Saturday but has not given an end time, so the bar fades out.

outages.name: Chase
outages.label: Morning to 6:30 p.m.
outages.note: Complaints began climbing Monday morning, Nov. 16, and passed 4,700 on Downdetector by about 1 p.m. Chase blamed a software bug in an on-premises hardware system, not an attack, and said transactions were posting normally by about 6:30 p.m. Eastern.

outages.name: United Airlines
outages.label: About 1 hr 40 min
outages.note: United delayed departures from just before 5 p.m. Eastern on Monday, Nov. 16, after a failure in the system pilots use to get aircraft weights. The airline resolved it about an hour and 40 minutes after pilots first reported problems.

outages.name: Apple
outages.label: About 2¾ hours
outages.note: Apple's services began failing at about 11:45 a.m. Eastern on Tuesday, Nov. 17. Users were signed out of iCloud and could not reach the App Store, Apple Pay or Apple Music, and Apple stores could not complete sales. Apple blamed an internal update, said it was not a cyberattack and said by about 2:30 p.m. that the problem was largely resolved.

outages.name: NSA Net
outages.label: Still down
outages.note: CNN reported Tuesday, Nov. 17, that NSA Net was down, with no evidence of a cyberattack. The NSA said it saw “temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance” and that mission-critical capabilities remained fully operational. Sources told CBS and The Wall Street Journal a software patch was the cause.

status_html: As of 4:51 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday, no outlet had reported NSA Net restored. In a statement to Al Jazeera and others, an NSA spokesperson said the agency “experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance,” that “some internal systems were affected” and that “mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational.” Sources told CBS News and The Wall Street Journal the cause was a software patch, and CNN’s sources said there was no evidence of a cyberattack.
notknown_html:
When the outage began, how many of the agency’s employees and sites are affected, what the maintenance involved and when the network will return. The NSA has not said whether it is related to any of the week’s other failures, and no official or major outlet has reported a link.

Whether AI played any part. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told Fox News on Monday that he believes “super intelligence” is behind the failures, repeating an unnamed tech-industry contact’s theory, while also saying they look individually unrelated and, with “98% certainty,” not a cyberattack. Microsoft, the FAA, Chase, Apple and the NSA have each given non-AI causes.

Not counted here: a separate cyberattack reported Tuesday, in which researcher Scott Helme found malicious code planted through the website tool Optimizely on sites of 178 organizations, including CNN and Zoom, built to steal visitors’ data rather than knock sites offline. No one has tied it to these outages. Also, Fox News reported smaller problems on Tuesday at Gmail and at Marriott's website and app, based on Downdetector reports. Neither company had confirmed an outage.

This story reflects reporting through 4:51 p.m. Eastern on Nov. 17 and is checked every hour; the chart’s last bar keeps growing until the NSA’s network is reported back.
